result:
Root cause: in `variants/bug06/tt.inc`, the `ttProbe` depth gate branched on Z instead of C after `cp (hl)`, inverting the comparison both ways — it rejected the valid equal-depth cutoffs (which made iterations 1+2 cost 652 frames against a 468-frame clock budget, so `clkBudgetExceeded` stopped deepening at iteration 2 for every level) and accepted invalid shallower ones.

Files touched:
- `variants/bug06/tt.inc` — the fix: `jr z,ttNoCut` → `jr c,ttNoCut` (one opcode byte, 0x28→0x38, same length).
- `variants/bug06/Makefile` — `SRC` omitted `perft.inc`, `zobrist.inc`, `tt.inc`, so editing tt.inc did not rebuild the tape; added them. Also wired the new test into `make test`.
- `variants/bug06/test_level_depth.py` — new regression test (executable).
- `FIX_NOTES.md`, `STATE.md` — new, at the workspace root.

Gate status:
- Reported symptom no longer reproduces — PASS. 48K: L2 f8f7/0, L3/L4/L5 d5e4/30. Middlegame: L2 d5g2/47, L3/L4/L5 d5g2/77. Exactly the report's expected tables; hc128 agrees with 48K on every case.
- `make test` — PASS, 6/6 checks, ~37 s.
- New test — PASS on the fixed build (16/16 assertions); FAILS with exit 1 on the pre-fix tape, naming all 7 wrong answers and all 3 identical L2/L3 pairs.
- Characterisation (57 cases) — PASS, 57 ok / 0 failed both before and after the fix, output byte-identical. It does not discriminate this bug; it served as the no-regression gate. Its default harness path points outside the workspace, so it needs `--harness harness`.
- Build reproducibility — PASS. `make clean && make` reproduces byte-for-byte; `chess.bin` still 13516 bytes; the tape differs from the pre-fix tape in exactly 2 bytes (0x2CE8 opcode, 0x351B checksum).
- Review round — PASS. One synchronous round, fresh agent, verdict "no defect in the fix," zero blocking findings; gate closed at round 1 of 3.

Knowingly left open (recorded in FIX_NOTES.md §5, not resolved):
- R2: every TT entry is stored with depth 1 — `ttStore` reads the global `ttCurDepth`, which descendants clobber (verified: 55 occupied slots after an L5 search, all depth 1). Pre-existing, conservative, outside the diff. Deliberately not fixed — repairing it would move the engine off the move/score table the bug report calls correct and off the characterisation baseline.
- R4: the endgame pins sit on a 3.2% timing margin (453 frames vs a 468-frame budget); a ~3.3% slower engine would make a correct build look unfixed. The test names this and says to check `aidIter` at 0xE0F4 first.
- R5: the L5 cases do not reach depth 5 — the clock stop ends deepening at iteration 3 for L3/L4/L5 alike, so the L5 pins are the L3 values by construction.
- R7/R8: stale `tt.inc` header comment (says 8 KB/1024 buckets at 0x6000; actually 4 KB/512 at 0xC000) and stale `nmCd`/`lmrReduced` globals around LMR — both pre-existing and unrelated.
- The report's claim that higher levels "visibly take longer" did not reproduce: the broken build is charged exactly 652 frames at levels 2, 3, 4 and 5 alike.

I corrected my own first write-up: it claimed iterations 3+ ran and were answered from stale entries. Measurement shows the broken build never starts iteration 3; that mechanism is real but was pre-empted by the clock stop. FIX_NOTES.md §2 now carries the measured account.
